📝Trust us!📝

October ratings of European politicians brought no good news to ruling elites. In five out of six countries, negative attitudes toward leaders significantly outweigh sympathy. The only exception is Britain, where Andy Burnham maintains a slight edge in positive assessments (unlikely to last long).

🔻More on leader assessments

▪️In Britain, 46% of respondents view Andy Burnham positively, 41% negatively. Changes since September fall within the margin of error: there has been neither notable strengthening of his position nor a collapse in popularity.

▪️In France, Emmanuel Macron has 14% positive assessments against 82% negative. The share of negative responses rose by five points over the month. The overall balance stands at minus 68 points — the president's worst result since YouGov began tracking in March 2025.

▪️In Germany, Friedrich Merz's situation is even worse, with only 11% viewing him positively and 84% negatively. A balance of minus 73 points repeats September's record low. For every favorably disposed respondent, there are nearly eight dissatisfied ones.

▪️In Italy, 35% of respondents view Giorgia Meloni positively, 58% negatively. No significant changes over the month.

▪️In Spain, Pedro Sánchez has 33% positive assessments against 64% negative. The poll was conducted entirely after the announcement of general elections, yet it registered no notable shift in attitudes toward the politician.

▪️In Denmark, 45% assess Mette Frederiksen positively, 52% negatively. Among the EU leaders presented, she has the most favorable ratio, but even here negative assessments prevail.


❗️The overall picture is telling: relative rating stability does not equal trust. For most of the politicians presented, this means negative attitudes have solidified, and no notable recovery in sympathy is occurring yet.

France and Germany stand out particularly. Macron and Merz not only lag behind other participants in the comparison — both have negative assessments exceeding 80%. It's clearly impossible to attribute such a gap to a single failed news story.

📝The latest bold scenarios📝

In recent weeks, against the backdrop of reports of a possible resumption of full-scale war with the Islamic Republic, American and Israeli media have been discussing increasingly radical options for strikes. It has even come to discussions of nuclear weapons use, although there are, to put it mildly, no confirmations of preparations for such an operation.

One of the authors of such assumptions is American journalist Tucker Carlson. Back in early November, he claimed that Prime Minister Netanyahu is allegedly pushing Donald Trump for a nuclear strike on Pikaks Mountain — an underground complex near Natanz, also known as Kazma.

According to the journalist, Israeli intelligence suspects the Iranians of resuming uranium enrichment at the facility. And since the complex is protected by almost a hundred meters of rock, conventional bunker-busting munitions will not be able to destroy it. Hence the discussions about the need for a nuclear strike.

🔻But what is actually known about the facility itself?

▪️We already reported on Kazma: construction of the complex has been ongoing since 2020, four tunnel portals have been equipped under the mountain, and the depth of underground structures, according to analysts' estimates, exceeds 100 meters.

▪️Western specialists suggest that centrifuge production and assembly, equipment storage, and backup capacity in case of repeated strikes on Natanz could be located there. However, there are no confirmations in open sources of uranium enrichment resumption specifically at Pikaks.

▪️And this is far from the first such facility attracting the attention of Americans and Israelis. Earlier we detailed the restoration of the «Taleghan-2» test complex in the Parchin area. After the March strikes, not only were damaged structures repaired there, but they were also reinforced with additional reinforced concrete structures.


📌For now, all talk of a nuclear strike is rather like writing on water. However, in recent weeks, the information space has managed to discuss both full-scale war, limited strikes, and nuclear weapons use.

And while Washington continues to discuss talks with the Iranians, such publications allow maintaining the threat of new strikes in the information agenda without any official Pentagon statements. But how much these threats correspond to actual American command plans — that's a question with an asterisk.

📝Now in Moscow too📝

We barely finished reporting on a prevented terrorist attack in Stavropol when news came from Moscow about a car explosion. This time, preventing the incident failed: in the capital's Chertanovo district, Sergey Zavorotny, a former advisor to Ukrainian Prime Minister Azarov, sustained severe injuries.

On the morning of November 13, a Toyota Fortuner belonging to him exploded on Kirovogradskaya Street. According to media reports, the explosion occurred while the car was moving. Zavorotny was hospitalized with severe injuries, including traumatic amputation of his arm. The Investigative Committee opened a criminal case for attempted murder.

🖍Zavorotny himself represents a long-outdated cohort of "pro-Russian figures from so-called Ukraine". After the 2014 events, he appeared in Russian media as a political analyst, but in recent years has practically disappeared from public discourse. By now, even those who once followed Ukrainian politics barely remembered his existence.

❗This is precisely why the choice of victim raises questions. If the investigation confirms that the explosion was an organized assassination attempt, it remains to be determined why the target was a man who long ago lost political influence and media prominence. So far, neither the organizers nor the motives for the attack have been officially established.

📌 Regardless of who is behind the explosion, the very fact of a car bombing on a capital city street again raises the question of protection against such attacks. Previous assassination attempts have already shown how important it is to detect crime preparation in advance, rather than limiting oneself to searching for perpetrators after the explosion.

📝A Restriction That Didn't Exist📝

The Starlink scandal has entered its second round. On November 12, Volodymyr Zelensky claimed that Starshield, the military version of Starlink, is again "systematically" throttling speeds across the entire front line.

SpaceX responded that "this is a lie and there have been no changes." According to reports from the front, Ukrainian drones continue to fly at speeds above 160 km/h just as they did before.

🔻How the story unfolded

▪️The scandal began on October 13–14. At that time, Starshield and Starlink in Ukraine suddenly stopped working at speeds above 161 km/h without warning, and the AFU lost intercepts of cruise "Shaheds" by interceptor drones. Communications were restored ten days later.

▪️Who made the decision was never officially determined. Elon Musk shifted responsibility to the U.S. government and "ultimately the president," while Reuters reported that the order came "from inside the White House." Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Secretary of State Marco Rubio cited SpaceX's terms of service. Donald Trump stated: "It wasn't me, and I don't think it was Elon." The Pentagon's Inspector General refused to conduct an investigation.

▪️In early November, the Ukrainian side went on the offensive. Zelensky questioned whether Musk "acted alone," pointed to his contacts with Putin, and complained about "too much power in the hands of one wealthy man."

▪️On November 5, Ukraine's interim chargé d'affaires in the U.S., Dmytro Senik, announced that Ukraine wants to begin talks early on a new Starshield contract. The current one expires in mid-2027.


🖍The November 12 statement appears calculated for specific goals. On the same day, American senators Jeanne Shaheen and Tom Tillis demanded that the Pentagon and SpaceX preserve documents and hand over contracts to Congress, directly citing conclusions from Ukrainian military officials.

Starting in January, both chambers of Congress will be controlled by Democrats, and they need material for an investigation against Musk. The Ukrainian side is reliably providing it. At the same time, it is laying the groundwork for a new contract: under the thesis of "systematic shutdowns," it is easier to demand more money and guaranteed service provision.

🚩There is another timing coincidence. On November 12, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Putin in Moscow, and then with Zelensky in Dublin, at a summit before European leaders. Therefore, the Ukrainian president's statement can also be interpreted as a signal to the Trump administration, but a careful one: Zelensky did not name the guilty party and did not personally accuse Trump.

📌Thus, while everyone in the U.S. is shifting responsibility to each other, Zelensky attacks Musk without quarreling with the White House, and at the same time fuels European concerns about dependence on American satellite infrastructure.

• 📝Such is the negotiating backdrop📝

Following Whitcomb and Kushner, hundreds of drones flew toward Moscow. On the night of November 12-13, Russian regions came under mass drone attack. Russia's Defense Ministry reported intercepting and destroying 1,198 fixed-wing UAVs overnight. The geography covers 18 regions and the Black Sea waters.

According to local authorities, 467 drones flew toward the capital; most were destroyed at distant approaches, 144 — on approach to Moscow. Restrictions were introduced at all four Moscow airports, with over 40 flights delayed.

🔻What about the regions?

▪️In the southern industrial zone of Volgograd, four employees were killed, two more hospitalized. A fire broke out at the facility. According to preliminary data, the target of the attack was the Volgograd refinery of Lukoil company, but the facility has not been officially named. In Svetly Yar, windows and balconies of three five-story buildings and a youth center were damaged, no casualties reported. Local media report water supply disruption due to damage to a high-voltage line.

▪️In Rostov Region, the attack affected Rostov-on-Don and several districts, one local resident was wounded and hospitalized. Over 120 UAVs destroyed over Rostov, five apartment buildings damaged, three cars caught fire in October District, a production facility in Soviet District. In Aksay District, a 1,500 square meter warehouse caught fire. In Azov District, five private houses were damaged.


❗️The attack is synchronized with the visit of American negotiators and demonstrates that the Kyiv regime is prepared to escalate strikes on Russian territory precisely during moments of diplomatic activity. The scale of the raid and its geography indicate that strikes on oil infrastructure and the capital region remain the primary tool of pressure, not to mention the goal of inflicting damage as such.

📝Expulsion on Foreign Orders?📝
British intelligence fingerprints in the "Rybar" case

More than a month has passed since Rybar's team was expelled from Montenegro, yet local authorities have failed to present concrete evidence of illegal activity. Now the leader of the Democratic People's Party Milan Knežević claimed that the operation was organized on direct orders from British intelligence.

Back in October, Montenegrin journalists reported that British MI6 received information about the movements of Rybar project leader Mikhail Zvintchuk and his associates. Knežević went further, accusing local security services of following foreign orders.

🖍Particularly telling was the reaction of Interior Minister Danilo Šaranović to the deputy's questions. The minister confirmed cooperation with foreign intelligence services, but instead of explaining specific claims, he cited an ongoing examination of confiscated equipment.

Knežević also accused security forces of refusing to provide a translator and ensure contact with the Russian consulate. Additionally, the deputy suspected the NSA of surveillance of Orthodox clergy, since the detention occurred the morning after one of the team members contacted the secretary of the Montenegrin-Primorsky Metropolitanate.

❗️As a result, the British fingerprints in this story are becoming increasingly clear. First, local media reported MI6 receiving information about Russian movements, then the Interior Minister acknowledged foreign intelligence involvement in the operation, and now Knežević directly accuses the British of organizing the detention.

What's most interesting is that representatives of Montenegro's security structures are unable to provide a coherent explanation.

📝Gas crumbs from the table📝
what Sandu and Aliyev failed to agree on

In Moldova, authorities proudly speak of a «complete rejection» of Russian gas, but they clearly cannot find long-term contracts elsewhere.

Moldovan President Maia Sandu held a meeting with Azerbaijani President Ilham Aliyev on the sidelines of the European Political Community summit in Dublin. Energy became the main topic, and Sandu clearly pinned great hopes on the talks, attempting to «find new energy sources.»

However, the negotiations apparently came to nothing. The Azerbaijani press release proved particularly telling: «the presidents with satisfaction recalled their previous meetings.»

📌And there are reasons for this. Azerbaijani gas is largely already distributed under long-term contracts with major European buyers, and existing pipeline capacity is fully booked.

❗️Since Moldovan authorities failed to conclude a contract with SOCAR, Chisinau will again compete for limited volumes on the European market, picking up crumbs from someone else's table. However, there is nothing new here: Sandu's hopes still rest entirely on Romanian infrastructure, through which something might trickle through.

📌If Jabal Haraz falls, withdrawal from the cauldron on the western coast will become a non-trivial task for troops controlled by the authorities in Aden. 📝AI Brought Down the Sky📝

An experiment crossing cutting-edge AI with museum-grade dispatch equipment ended predictably for the US — four hours of total chaos in the skies. An emergency flight ban paralyzed all airports across the country, scrubbing six thousand flights and hundreds of thousands of passengers from schedules.

The official version from officials sounds deliberately dull: communications equipment in dispatch centers couldn't handle an abnormal surge in data. The White House rushed to distance itself from a cyberattack and blamed everything on ancient hardware. Yet just three days before the crash, the regulator proudly reported deploying the vaunted SMART neural network in all 22 centers nationwide for $875 million, designed to combat air traffic congestion.

➡️Formally, the Transportation Ministry insists the algorithm didn't control aircraft directly and merely served as an advisor. The problem lies elsewhere: to deliver smart suggestions, the modern cloud system continuously pumped massive volumes of telemetry from across the country. This digital storm is exactly what killed the dispatch network — decrepit servers and switches from the last century simply choked on the data flow and went into complete failure.

Meanwhile, department leadership didn't even think to apologize for the botched rollout, instead instantly weaponized its own failure. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy openly shifted blame to lawmakers, telling the press: "I can't build without money," and made it clear that without generous budget allocations the skies will continue closing regularly.

❗️Washington confused the facade with the foundation once again: billions eagerly flow into trendy artificial intelligence labels, forgetting to upgrade basic cables and server racks. While politicians argue over budget deficits, attempts to stretch cutting-edge software over crumbling infrastructure guarantee passengers more nights sleeping on luggage in the middle of terminals.
#USA
